request.spec:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box (and any later import) are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not
clash (and leaves no clashing alias).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box (and any later import) are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not
clash (and leaves no clashing alias).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A name or alias can no longer be used on a sheet if any other sheet in its tree already uses it as a name or alias. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. Since then I've only changed comments in two endpoint YAML files and haven't re-run it.

**What counts as the tree:** a sheet's ancestors (parent, grandparent and so on) and all of its descendants, limited to sheets that exist. Sibling sheets aren't included. The lookup is a new `tree()` method in `setting/SettingStore.java`.

**What is now refused:**
- **Adding a person:** the name is refused if it's used anywhere in the tree (`CheckNameFree`).
- **Adding an alias:** same rule (`AddAlias`).
- **Quick-add bar:** if the name matches someone on this sheet, the claim goes to them as before. If it would add a new person whose name is used elsewhere in the tree, it's refused before anything is stored (`FindOrAddPerson`).
- **Paste box:** no change was needed. A paste can only name people already on the sheet, so a name that exists only on another sheet in the tree was already refused.
- **Transfer:** I treated transfer as the "later import" in the request, since there's no separate import feature. A transfer is now refused if the person's name or an alias is used in the destination sheet's tree. The sheet they're leaving isn't counted, because their names go with them.
- **Editing through the person form:** refused if the new name is used in the tree, or if any of the person's aliases is (`CheckNameFreeForEdit`). So a clashing person can't be edited until they're renamed to a name that doesn't clash and none of their aliases clash either.

**Clashing column:** each person row has a new `person-clashing` cell showing `yes` or `no`. It's worked out each time the person is fetched from the sheet tree as it stands now, not stored. In as-of views it also uses today's tree.

**Things to be aware of:**
- Setting a sheet's parent never checks for clashes; people who clash afterwards just show clashing yes. The tests rely on this.
- The edit rule means a person whose only clash is an alias can't be edited through the person form at all, because the form can't remove aliases. That's how I read "leaves no clashing alias".
- The spec never actually checks for a `yes` value, so that display isn't covered by the tests.

I also updated the doc comments on the add-person and edit-person endpoints.
